Misconception.description: The error occurs when inequalities are graphed with solid lines regardless of whether they are inclusive. Misunderstanding leads to incorrectly including or excluding the boundary in the solution set.
Misconception.title: Inclusive vs. Exclusive Boundaries

Misconception.description: Errors arise when students do not correctly clear fractions from equations. This may lead to unnecessary complexity or incorrect combining of terms, causing inaccurate solutions.
Misconception.title: Failure to Clear Fractions

successIndicators: Check order of (x, y) in solutions
Misconception.description: In solving systems of equations, students swap x and y coordinates, leading to incorrect solutions. This misunderstanding results from confusion over variable placement in the ordered pair.
Misconception.title: Switching X and Y Coordinates

successIndicators: Identify boundary line as dashed or solid
Misconception.description: Some students interpret the coefficients in inequalities as the slope without converting them to slope-intercept form. This leads them to graph equations with incorrect slopes, resulting in misrepresentation of inequalities.
Misconception.title: Incorrect Slope Conversion
